A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RapTB/SubM work and provide complete, comparable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. All 20 appendix pages match in text and rendering after excluding page numbers.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on SMILES, Expr24, CommonGen, and antimicrobial peptide generation, together with ablations and model-scaling results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix F retain the same rooted-prefix objective, absorbed suffix targets, auxiliary termination stop-gradients, and SubM replay-selection procedure.

E1.justification: The same SMILES, Expr24, CommonGen, and antimicrobial peptide tasks and longer-horizon scenarios are retained. The added citations in Section 4.1 introduce no evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including PPO/GRPO, TB/SubTB, RootSubTBLogZ, AvgPrefixTB, and the AMP baselines. Replay comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Model configurations, training budgets, decoding constraints, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C, E, and G, including 3,200 SMILES and 6,400 Expr24 samples per run.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical component ablations, prefix and termination diagnostics, longer-horizon analyses, CommonGen examples, and hyperparameter sensitivity studies, including Table 6 and Appendices A, D, and F.1.

E5.justification: Both retain 95% confidence intervals, six runs for the SMILES summary in Table 7, three seeds for Expr24 in Table 18, and the same Student-t interval formula in Appendix E.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 retains RapTB+SubM accuracy 0.988, score 0.844, and FPDiv 0.898 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, fixed-point qualification and bound in Section 3.4, submodular construction in Section 3.5, and derivations in Appendix F are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about prefix collapse, length bias, RapTB/SubM contributions, and generalization across tasks and model scales.

C2.justification: Interpretations of replay coverage and termination drift are unchanged, as are the absorption-bias qualification in Section 3.4 and the downstream molecular-validation caveat in the Impact Statement.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract statement announcing released code and supplies a specific ChemGFN repository address absent from v2. Existing implementation and hyperparameter documentation remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds seven cited works and bibliography entries through the molecular-generation and drug-likeness passages in Section 4.1. Section 2 and the core novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are limited to the abstract's code-release sentence and citation insertions in Section 4.1. The remaining prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The additions cause localized text reflow and extend the bibliography onto another page, shifting appendix pagination. Figures, table structures, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new abstract repository address provides a concrete implementation-access pointer that v2 lacks, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Added citations and layout changes leave the scientific evidence unchanged. The PDFs establish the improved access information, but do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.
